newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran appeals for help for Kurdish refugees.
newsitem.headline: Iran appeals for help for Kurdish refugees.

text.p: Iran warned on Sunday of miserable winter conditions facing tens of thousands of Kurdish refugees who fled from Iraq to Iran and appealed for international help.

The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted a Red Crescent official as saying that with winter approaching "life could become a misery" for the refugees "if they are to stay longer in the temporary camps."
"He called on international bodies and organisations to provide necessary relief assistance and help resolve the issue of the tens of thousands of Kurds," IRNA said.
Iran on Tuesday told European envoys the refugees faced bleak winter conditions at their mountainous camps and held the international community responsible for their plight.

On Wednesday Iran said 1,000 more Kurdish refugees had crossed into its territory on Tuesday, to join tens of thousands who had fled northern Iran since its takeover by a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction in September.
Fighting between the two rival Kurdish factions broke out again at the weekend.

Iran, which said in late September it was sheltering 65,000 Kurdish refugees, has criticised international organisations, saying they were not providing enough help for the refugees living in tent camps in the cold mountainous border region.
